::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** July 10. 1865  
**Manuscript:** Copy outletter book British Library Add MSS. 55384 (2): P. 647
:::

Dear Miss Yonge	
[Mr Maclear](people/person_937.qmd)’s address is

Rev G. F. M. 24 Elgin Crescent
Kensington Park Gardens[[footnote:1]

Many thanks for your kind [*illegible*] about the [illustrations](organizations/other_167.qmd). [I](people/person_939.qmd)think on the whole it would be dangerous to employ an unpractised pencil.[^1] On some future occasion I shall be very glad indeed.

My people at home have been reading your [cameos](cmy_books/cmybook_73.qmd), and think they would make a nice book.[^2] I am inclined to think so too - in a cheap form

Yours ever truly
A. Macmillan

---

[^1]: A letter is missing, dated between 4 and 10 July 1865, in which CMY evidently asked for Maclear's address.
[^2]: CMY had tried to persuade him to use [Katie Johns](people/person_887.qmd) as illustrator of *The Prince and the Page*.
[^3]: CMY had been producing “Cameos from English History” for the *MP* since the beginning of 1851, and 70 had appeared by the time of this letter.
